title: Networking for Cloud & DevOps
subtitle: The networking a developer or DevOps engineer needs to deploy and debug services
audience_line: Developers, DevOps and cloud engineers without a networking background
overview: This workshop gives developers and DevOps engineers the networking they meet every day when they deploy and debug services. Participants work through IP addressing and subnetting, DNS, HTTP and TLS, routing, NAT, firewalls and VPNs, then load balancers, reverse proxies and CDNs, with their cloud equivalents, always with the command-line tools used to check each layer. The workshop closes with a final project: a multi-tier web deployment with injected faults, which participants diagnose and repair.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Developers, DevOps and cloud engineers without a networking background

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: None. Comfort with a Linux terminal helps (course: Linux & Bash Scripting). No networking knowledge needed

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 18 h: 15 h of chapters + 3 h buffer

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Workshop: short lectures, each followed by hands-on exercises at the command line

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: Runs locally: one laptop per participant (8 GB RAM, Docker) running a multi-tier web stack in containers prepared by the trainer (DNS server, load balancer, web and database tiers); no cloud account or cost

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: Exercises validated during each phase and a final troubleshooting project; certificate of completion for participants who complete both

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can read a network path from client to service, plan subnets, and find and fix DNS, TLS, routing, firewall and load-balancer faults with standard tools

phases.name: Network Foundations
phases.focus: TCP/IP, IPv4 addressing and subnetting, DNS, HTTP and TLS
phases.intro: Participants build the mental model used for the rest of the workshop: layers, addresses and subnets, then the application protocols that every web service depends on. Validated exercise: a subnet plan for a three-tier application, and a request traced from DNS lookup to TLS handshake to HTTP response.

chapters.title: TCP/IP Essentials
chapters.content: OSI and TCP/IP models, Ethernet, IPv4 addressing, subnetting, CIDR

chapters.title: Application Protocols
chapters.content: DNS, HTTP and HTTPS, TLS and certificates

phases.name: Routing, Traffic & Troubleshooting
phases.focus: Routing, NAT, firewalls, load balancing and diagnostic tools
phases.intro: Participants follow traffic across routers, NAT and firewalls, see how load balancers, reverse proxies and CDNs spread it across servers, then practise a layer-by-layer troubleshooting method with the standard Linux tools. Validated exercise: a packet capture that shows why a request through the load balancer fails.

chapters.title: Routing & Edges
chapters.content: Routing, NAT, firewalls, VPN basics; cloud equivalents: VPC subnets, route tables, security groups

chapters.title: Traffic Management
chapters.content: Layer 4 and layer 7 load balancing, reverse proxies, CDN; managed cloud load balancers

chapters.title: Troubleshooting
chapters.content: ip, ss, dig, curl, traceroute, tcpdump

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: Diagnose and repair a broken multi-tier deployment
phases.intro: Teams of two receive a multi-tier web deployment in which the trainer has injected faults, find each fault with the tools from the workshop, fix it and explain it to the group.

chapters.title: Brief & Diagnosis
chapters.content: Read the incident report, map the deployment, locate the faults layer by layer

chapters.title: Fix & Debrief
chapters.content: Fix the DNS, TLS, load-balancer and firewall faults, write the incident notes, present root causes to the group

project.title: Broken Deployment Rescue
project.brief: A multi-tier web deployment that does not answer: participants trace the path from client to database, find the injected DNS, TLS, load-balancer and firewall faults, and restore the service.
project.stack: Linux, Docker, CoreDNS, HAProxy, Nginx, OpenSSL, ip, ss, dig, curl, traceroute, tcpdump
project.deliverable: Working deployment, incident notes with root cause for each fault
